items.q: What are the minimal free peritoneal fluid volumes required sequentially for ultrasonographic detection, clinical shifting dullness, and eliciting a fluid thrill?
items.exp: Peritoneal fluid detection thresholds are: <100 mL on ultrasonography (USG), 500 mL on clinical examination for shifting dullness, and 1.5 L for elicitation of a fluid thrill. (Book p1007)

items.q: By definition in decompensated chronic liver disease, refractory ascites refers to peritoneal fluid accumulation that exhibits:
opts: No therapeutic response to maximum doses of diuretic medications
Persistent recurrence despite weekly large-volume paracenteses
Secondary bacterial infection following diagnostic paracentesis
Development of acute intrinsic tubular necrosis during diuretics
items.exp: Refractory ascites is defined as peritoneal fluid accumulation that shows no response to maximum doses of diuretics (spironolactone up to 400 mg/day plus furosemide up to 160 mg/day). (Book p1007)

items.q: Following large-volume paracentesis (LVP) for tense ascites, which adjunctive intervention should routinely be administered to preserve effective circulating volume?
items.exp: Large volume paracentesis (LVP) should be followed by intravenous albumin replacement to prevent post-paracentesis circulatory dysfunction, noted in text as expensive. (Book p1007)

items.q: Match each diagnostic modality for ascitic fluid detection with its corresponding minimum fluid threshold: 1. Ultrasonography (USG) 2. Shifting dullness 3. Fluid thrill
items.exp: Ultrasonography detects free fluid at volumes <100 mL; clinical shifting dullness requires 500 mL; elicitation of a fluid thrill requires 1.5 L of peritoneal fluid. (Book p1007)

items.q: A 52-year-old man with decompensated alcoholic cirrhosis presents with massive abdominal distension. On examination, a prominent fluid thrill is elicited. Based on physical diagnostic thresholds, what is the minimum volume of free ascitic fluid present?
opts: At least 1.5 L of free peritoneal fluid
Around 500 to 750 mL of peritoneal fluid
Strictly less than 100 mL of fluid
items.exp: A fluid thrill requires at least 1.5 L of free peritoneal fluid to be elicited clinically. Shifting dullness requires 500 mL, whereas USG can detect volumes <100 mL. (Book p1007)
